maya: heads-up — after the selector rollout (v2.3) I'm seeing a ~12% drop in token/sec on INT4 paths when continuous batching + KV reuse is enabled. FP8 path looks stable. :eyes:

arjun: can you paste the pprof / flamegraph output? any particular kernel hotspots?

maya: minimal profile pasted below — ran a 1h canary with synthetic chat workload: average batch size 6, median seq len 128. Command: `./run_perf.sh --workload chat_continuous --selector v2.3 --quant int4`

```
# hotspot summary (sample counts)
matmul_small_shape               34%
kv_concat_dequantize            21%
attn_kv_read                    12%
softmax                          8%
other                            25%
```

maya: attaching brief batch-shape histogram: `{seq_len:count}` -> `{32:1200, 64:3400, 128:9200, 256:1800}`. There's a fat tail at 128 which seems to hit the int4 kernel shape boundary.

liam: hm — matches a kernel-selection edge case. INT4 kernels currently choose a small-shape matmul for padded shapes >128 and <=192 which has poor occupancy for our GPU config. FP8 uses a fused packed-kernel that tolerates padding better.

sasha: do we know the pad granularity? int4 path pads to multiple of 32 bits -> effectively seqpad to multiple-of-8 tokens? that can blow up compute for mid-sized batches.

maya: confirmed — int4 path pads to 8-token granularity. For median 128 it's fine but for the 64->128 transitions padding waste spikes with continuous batching because we merge short and long requests.

perf-bot: microbench numbers: baseline (fp8, selector v2.2): 185k tokens/s; canary (int4, selector v2.3): 162k tokens/s; delta = -12.4%. Mem usage +3% due to extra KV buffer copies.

arjun: two hypotheses: (1) selector is choosing int4 kernel despite high pad waste; (2) KV concat/dequant stage is doing an extra pass for int4 calibration metadata. Can someone repro with `--trace-kernel-selection`?

maya: running now with trace. sample output: `selector->matmul: int4_small_shape chosen; pad_waste=28% ; fallback_check=false; kv_cache_reuse=true`

liam: that pad_waste number explains it. Proposed fixes: (A) adjust selector to bias toward fp8 when pad_waste > 20% for kernels where int4 occupancy falls below threshold; (B) add a pad-trim micro-optimization: trim trailing zeros before doing matmul and re-pad after (cheap for our kernel layout); (C) re-evaluate calibration step so kv_concat_dequantize is inlined (reduce memcpy).

sasha: (B) sounds promising — on paper it reduces total MACs without touching quantization scales. microbench?

arjun: bench: locally ran int4 with pad-trim enabled -> tokens/s +7% vs int4 baseline, still -6% vs fp8 baseline. Memory copies reduced by ~35%. Code snippet I used:

```
# pseudo
for batch in batches:
  trim_len = compute_trim(batch)
  x = slice(x, :trim_len)  # avoid padded matmul
  out = int4_matmul(x)
  out = pad_back(out)
```

maya: will flip pad-trim on in canary flag `int4_pad_trim=true` and run A/B (10m windows).

liam: also flag to selector: `pad_waste_threshold` so we can experiment with automatic fallback to fp8 for high pad waste cases.

perf-bot: quick note — calibration: we saw extra per-call scale/unscale for KV when switching kernels; ensure quant metadata isn't stored per-slice causing extra memcpy.

sasha: ping @arjun for calibration script that updates KV quant params post-selector-change. we should include that in the rollback checklist if perf doesn't improve.

maya: thanks — I'll attach full traces and flamegraphs to the thread once the canary finishes. planning to run 2h A/B and then decide on selector tweak vs. pad-trim permanent opt. :thumbsup:
